content:
sam: Heads-up — saw a sizable regression in prefix cache reuse on Private VPC after last runtime rollout (v2.14.0). p95 generate latency jumped and cache hit-rate is much lower than Hosted.
meera: can you share the numbers and which customers/profiles are affected?
sam: quick snapshot: Hosted (prod-us) hit_rate=86.0% vs Private-custA (vpc) hit_rate=61.2%. traffic ~130r/s each. cache_evictions up ~4x for the private workers. p50 110ms -> 155ms, p95 220ms -> 420ms.
jon: I grabbed a short pprof sample on the private worker during the spike (30s window):
jon: ```
jon: 45%  kernel_selector()
jon: 25%  kv_cache_lookup()
jon: 10%  memcpy()
jon: 8%   wait_io()
jon: 5%   mutex_spin()
jon: ```
jon: kernel_selector is firing often because a subset of sequences are taking a slower fallback kernel (quantized path) on those hosts.
luis: note: v2.14.0 changed batching defaults for private profiles to reduce OOM risk on smaller GPU machines — max_batch_tokens 4096->2048 and batching_delay lowered. That fragments groups of similar short-prefixed requests, reducing temporal locality (fewer co-batched prefixes).
sam: also found a config mismatch: Hosted uses cache.collapse_whitespace=false (legacy behavior) while some private configs had it enabled during the recent config propagation. that leads to different key bytes for the same logical prompt. example: 
 sam: ```
 sam: // hosted key gen
 sam: key = hash(prefix + "\\n" + user_ctx)
 sam: // private (collapse_whitespace=true)
 sam: key = hash(collapse_ws(prefix) + "\\n" + user_ctx)
 sam: ```
meera: that would explain deterministic misses for prefixes that differ only in incidental spacing. storage layer (NFS vs local SSD) could amplify misses too if lookup latency causes timeouts/evictions.
olivia: mitigation ideas (short-term):
 - align cache keying flags across environments (set collapse_whitespace=false for affected VPCs)
 - run a prefix_warmup preheat job to populate hot keys for 24-48h
 - enable sticky_shard routing for customer flows so repeated sessions hit same worker and benefit from local KV cache
 - temporarily relax eviction pressure (increase per-worker cache size) for impacted pool
infra-bot: Rollout started: https://ci.redwood/runtime/deploys/1145 (runtime/v2.14.1 with config patch)
deploy-bot: Canary healthy for 30m ✅ no increase in OOMs, latency subset stable.
sam: kicked off bench run: tools/bench/hitrate.py --target=private-custA --duration=600 --trace-keys=20; excerpt below:
sam: ```
 sam: total=72000
 sam: hits=43920 (61.0%)
 sam: misses=28080
 sam: top_missed_prefixes=["/search?q=long-term","/compose/meeting_notes_template_7"]
 sam: avg_key_length=142
 sam: ```
meera: can you also pull batching metrics (batch_size histogram) to confirm fragmentation? query: http://metrics:9090/api/v1/query?query=batch_size_bucket
luis: I inspected logs — private workers serving from NFS show higher kv lookup latency and occasional EIO spikes; local-SSD workers have much lower kv latency and higher effective reuse. lock contention correlates with slower storage responses.
olivia: rollout plan I recommend: 1) quick config alignment (collapse_whitespace=false) for affected VPCs, 2) run prefix_warmup for 48h, 3) enable sticky_shard routing for 72h on canary then expand, 4) add CT to detect keying config drift between Hosted/Dedicated/Private. :eyes:
jon: filed issue: https://git.redwood/r/runtime/issues/1298 (config-diff CT + regression test for cache keying)
meera: applied config patch to custA (normalize flag toggled) and kicked warmup. monitoring shows improvement within 2–3 hours: private-custA hit_rate -> 78.9%, p95 down to ~260ms. still ~6 points behind Hosted but much better.
sam: agreed long-term we should: unify default keying, surface config diffs in Console, and add a "cache warmup" orchestration when configs change.
olivia: will draft a short RFC for the CT + diff check.
sam: thanks all — marking for retro and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
